devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Marriage is protected because covenant matters to God.

Adultery is not merely a private failure of self-control. It is the breaking of a
promise made before God, and it wounds a spouse, children, and a wider community.
The Bible treats it seriously because it treats faithfulness seriously.

Jesus again goes to the root: "anyone who looks at a woman lustfully has already
committed adultery with her in his heart" (Matt 5:28). He is not saying that
attraction is sin, or that noticing beauty is adultery. He is addressing the
deliberate cultivation of desire for someone who is not ours, the fantasy we
choose to feed.

That teaching lands differently in an age of screens, where such material is
constantly available and privately consumed. Many sincere Christians struggle
here, often in shame and silence.

If that is you, hear two things. First, this is serious, and pretending otherwise
helps no one. Second, there is no sin here that Christ's blood does not cover,
and confession to a trusted believer is often where freedom begins (Jas 5:16).

Notice also that God uses marriage as His picture of His own faithfulness to us
(Eph 5:31-32). That is why unfaithfulness grieves Him. It defaces a portrait of
His own covenant love.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something you are feeding privately that you would not want known?
2. Who could you speak to honestly this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, make me faithful in heart as well as action. Where I am struggling, give
me courage to bring it into the light. Amen.
